findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There is observed to be a gap in the bottom right corner of the back door. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that this gap is closed to prevent the entry of insects and rodents.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:

2. FIRST REPEAT- The table under the soda machines in the back. 
3. The table under the iced coffee machine. 
4. Inside of the cabinets under the soda machines. 

This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was a mop bucket observed to still have used mop water in it. CORRECTED- The PIC dumped the waste water in the mop sink during the inspection. Ensure that this waste water is immediately discarded of after use in the mop sink.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The facility is observed to have two coolers under the main counter that holds all of the hot holding for customers. There is a cooler on each side of the counter. These coolers had previously been used to hold food items such as hot dogs. The PIC stated that they continuously had issues with each cooler and are not using them. The PIC stated that they might be sending in a new cooler to replace one of them. The facility has enough cold holding to not need these coolers. Ensure that these coolers are either replaced or removed if they are not going to be in use. The facility should be free of equipment that is no longer functioning or used.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The soda nozzles were observed to be soiled with an accumulation of debris. All equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils should be cleaned to sight and touch. Ensure that the soda nozzles are cleaned and then are maintained cleaned. The nozzles of the latte machine were also observed to be soiled. Ensure that these are cleaned and then maintained cleaned. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The display cooler at the front of the store was observed to be stacked past the point of refrigeration. There were many TCS (Time/Temperature Control for Safety) foods that were out of temperature in the cooler. These items include but are not limited to: Peanut Butter & Jelly sandwiches (48-54F), a salad (54F), charcuterie packs (47-54F), buffalo chicken wraps (50-53F), breakfast sandwiches (49F), and Bomb Burritos (46-50F). These items were voluntarily discarded during the inspection. All items discarded were between 46F and 60F. Ensure that this cooler is not over stocked to allow proper refrigeration. Stocking non-TCS items in the corners is highly recommended. Ensure that the temperatures of items in this cooler are frequently checked and avoid over stocking. 

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: There was not a thermometer in the hot dog cooler under the roller or in the walk-in cooler. There should always be a thermometer in refrigerated or hot food storage units. During the inspection, a thermometer was placed in both coolers. 

 (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature.

findings.comment:
3-307.11: Water bottles cases were observed stored outside near the wall of the establishment. This is not considered a clean, dry location for the water bottles. Ensure the water bottles are moved to a clean, dry location where they are protected from possible contamination.

  FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306.

 (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The following areas were soiled. These areas need to be cleaned and then maintained cleaned: 

1. Under the slushy machine had an accumulation of soil and a disposable cup was being used to catch drips. Cease use of this cup and clean under the machine. 
2. There is a piece of equipment for fresh toppings that is located on the counter across from the soda fountain. This piece of equipment is soiled and has empty containers in it that have date markings that state to discard product by 3/30/2024. Ensure that this piece of equipment is cleaned or put away if it is no longer being used. 
3. Inside the cabinets under the soda fountain has an accumulation of debris. Ensure that this area is cleaned and maintained cleaned. 
4. There is a build up of ice on the back wall of the hot dog cooler. Ensure that this ice is cleaned to allow the cooler to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
5. The floor in the back area is in need of a general cleaning, especially behind shelves and around the back of the drink machines. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.comment:
6-501.11: There is a tile under the triple sink that has come off of the floor. Ensure that this tile is repaired and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 

 PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There was no Certified Food Protection Manager at the establishment at the start of the inspection. Ensure a CFPM is at the establishment during all hours of food preparation. This includes when hot holding of foods is occurring. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Motor oil, antifreeze and other chemicals are stored next to and close to sugar, coffee, and other food or food contact surfaces (like paper towels and cups). Ensure these chemicals are stored in a location to prevent potential contamination of food. Additionally, a barrier can be put between chemicals and food so spilled chemicals cannot contaminate food. The oil and antifreeze were moved over a few inches to avoid possible contamination. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Water bottles cases were observed stored outside near the wall of the establishment. This is not considered a clean, dry location for the water bottles. Ensure the water bottles are moved to a clean, dry location where they are protected from possible contamination. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.
